external.title: Announcing Aster - a home for researchers on the open web

record.text:
The modern research ecosystem of online tools and communities is controlled by for-profit companies.

But we think that researchers should be the priority - not the product.

So, we're announcing Aster ID: not-for-profit Atmosphere account hosting for researchers.

record.text: Thank you for coming to today’s Apple event! You can find these and more Apple products at your nearest grocery store, farmers’ market, or orchard.

Welcome to the ONLY event about Apple happening today, as far as we know.

We'll be running this as an AMAAA (Ask Me Anything About Apples).

Ask your biggest Apple questions in the replies to this post and one of our Apple Geniuses will be with you shortly. 🍎
@lightlyspicy.bsky.social asks, "Best way to care for young apple trees?"

value.text: A few starters: keep them watered in dry weather. Protect them against any local predators (deer, rabbits, voles, toddlers etc.) and remove any fruit in the first year or two to help them establish stronger root systems.

@bestpaulever.bsky.social asks, "Why aren't there any blue apples?"

images.alt: Watercolor of a nearly purple striped red apple. It is dark red with blue-purple stripes. It is shown once whole and once cut stem to blossom-end).

Watercolor of a deep red apple, so red it is nearly purple. It is shiny and round. It is shown twice, once whole and once cut stem to blossom end. The core line is quite wide and the tube at the blossom end is long with the core lines meeting it at the calyx.

value.text: There are some red apples that are nearly blue. Blue Pearmain, Arkansas Black, and Robert's Crab for example. (the real answer is pigments and the limited variety that apples make)
